局.meaning: A <part>flag</part> hangs over the door of a busy office where clerks stamp forms all day. The rule is strict: say what you want in one <part>phrase</part>, one breath, or go to the back of the line. Stamp! Next! Welcome to the <kanji>bureau</kanji>.
局.on: The bureau's front desk is just a tiny <sound>kio</sound>sk, and a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo pops out of it to stamp your form.
局.kun: Upstairs, a court lady sneezes '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' over her <sound>bo</sound>nsai and catches the falling leaves in a <sound>ne</sound>t: a lady of the court.

数.meaning: A <part>rice carrier</part> stacks sack after sack on her head, and her friend taps each one with a folded <part>fan</part>: one, two, three, forty-one… The stack wobbles up into the clouds, and the whole market shouts out the <kanji>number</kanji>.
数.on: A <sound>su</sound>perhero swoops past the top of the stack and counts every sack in a blink.
数.kun: Down in the pond, a <sound>ca</sound>rp tries to count the <sound>zu</sound>cchini floating past and loses track at seven.

換.meaning: A sailor trades his <part>anchor</part> for a kid's <part>jack-in-the-box</part>. Boing! The toy springs open, the kid sails off with the anchor, and ten minutes later they both want their own back. Swap, swap again: they <kanji>interchange</kanji> them all afternoon.
換.on: On the last swap, the jack-in-the-box pops up holding a pink <sound>car</sound>nation.
換.kun: In the end the sailor changes his mind one more time and swaps the toy for a <sound>ca</sound>rp in a bucket.

度.meaning: In an old <part>shed</part>, a baker sets a <part>pretzel</part> on a <part>tray</part> and stares at the oven dial. Too cool and it's raw; too hot and it's charcoal. He turns the knob a hair at a time, counting the <kanji>degrees</kanji>.
度.on: A <sound>do</sound>lphin pokes its head through the shed window and flips the dial up ten more.
度.kun: Each time a pretzel burns, he dunks it in a <sound>tu</sound>b of water, and a <sound>bee</sound>tle swims out.

舌.meaning: Out of a <part>mouth</part> pokes something pink, covered in a <part>thousand</part> tiny bumps. It wiggles, it licks an ice lolly, it tastes the salt and the sugar, then it hides again behind the teeth. It's your <kanji>tongue</kanji>.
舌.on: Your tongue touches the <sound>ze</sound>st of a lemon and you sneeze so hard: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!'
舌.kun: Stick your tongue out at a knight and he hides behind his <sound>shi</sound>eld, then ducks into a <sound>tu</sound>b.

話.meaning: Grandpa starts a bedtime <part>speech</part> and his <part>tongue</part> runs away with him: dragons, pirates, a goat that can fly. Hours later the kids are snoring and he is still going. It's one very long <kanji>tale</kanji>.
話.on: The goat in the story cries '<sound>Wa</sound>h!' every time a dragon swoops down.
話.kun: In the tale, the goat sits in a <sound>hu</sound>t eating <sound>na</sound>an and talking with its mouth full.

救.meaning: Far out at sea, a swimmer shouts one <part>request</part>: 'Help!' On the beach, a lifeguard flaps open a giant <part>fan</part>, and the gust blows the swimmer all the way to shore. Dry sand, warm towel: <kanji>salvation</kanji>.
救.on: For the last stretch, the lifeguard hooks him out of the shallows with a long pool <sound>cue</sound>.
救.kun: A <sound>su</sound>shi chef and a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo grab his arms and pull him out of the surf.

平.meaning: A goat with little <part>horns</part> climbs onto a <part>drying rack</part> and tests each bar with its hooves. The left end dips, so it hops right; the right end dips, so it hops left. At last both bars sit level: perfectly <kanji>even</kanji>.
平.on: To keep it balanced for good, the goat spreads <sound>hay</sound> along both bars.
平.kun: Then the goat irons a crumpled <sound>tie</sound> on the rack until it lies flat.

不.meaning: Under a flat <part>one</part> brim stands a <part>pole</part> of a man, one arm a <part>slash</part>, the other a <part>dot</part>, frowning. Sunshine? Too hot. Cake? Too sweet. Whatever you say, he says no. He's always <kanji>negative</kanji>.
不.on: He won't even get up off his <sound>fu</sound>ton: 'No, no, no.'

難.meaning: A <part>husband</part> crawls through tall <part>grass</part> with a crumb in his <part>mouth</part>, trying to tempt a <part>sparrow</part>. Every time he gets close, it hops away. Three hours, no bird, grass in his ears. This is <kanji>difficult</kanji>.
難.on: At last he holds out a whole puffy <sound>naan</sound>, and the sparrow flies off with that too.
難.kun: He tries tempting it with a <sound>ca</sound>rp in a <sound>tu</sound>b, but the sparrow only laughs: too hard.

的.meaning: An archer paints a <part>white</part> ring on a board and uses a tiny <part>scoop</part> to dab a dot of red paint in the middle. She steps back, draws her bow and… thunk. Right in the <kanji>bull's eye</kanji>.
的.on: She snaps a photo and sends it as a <sound>tex</sound>t message: 'Got it!'
的.kun: Her next target is a <sound>mu</sound>g balanced on top of a <sound>to</sound>tem pole.

号.meaning: A coach cups his <part>mouth</part> and yells across the field. The kids line up in <part>one</part> row, each with a scarf <part>wrap</part>ped round their neck and a word sewn on it: Speedy, Rocket, Noodle. He calls out each <kanji>nickname</kanji>.
号.on: The <sound>go</sound>at on the team is nicknamed Lightning, though it only ever walks.
号.kun: The coach shouts so loudly that a <sound>sa</sound>rdine flies out of his lunchbox and lands in the <sound>ke</sound>tchup.

盗.meaning: At a buffet, a sneaky guest slides one <part>dish</part> into his coat, then the <part>next</part>, then the next. By dessert the table is bare and his coat clinks when he walks. He came to eat, but stayed to <kanji>steal</kanji>.
盗.on: On his way out he stubs his <sound>toe</sound> on the door, and a plate drops out of his sleeve.
盗.kun: He hides in a dark <sound>noo</sound>k and gobbles the <sound>su</sound>shi he took.

図.meaning: A pirate draws a big <part>cage</part> of a border on a sheet of paper, snips out the coastline with <part>scissors</part>, and sticks a burst of <part>fireworks</part> where the gold is buried. X marks the spot on his <kanji>map</kanji>.
図.on: He digs and digs, and the treasure turns out to be one giant <sound>zu</sound>cchini.
図.kun: He plans the whole trip from a beach <sound>hu</sound>t, with his pet <sound>ca</sound>rp watching from its bowl.

書.meaning: Sitting out in the <part>sun</part>, a girl dips her <part>brush</part> in ink and swishes stroke after stroke down the page. The ink dries as fast as she makes it. Page after page, all day long, she loves to <kanji>write</kanji>.
書.on: She sells her pages in a little <sound>sho</sound>p round the corner.
書.kun: One day she runs out of paper and writes a poem on the scales of a <sound>ca</sound>rp.

仕.meaning: A <part>gentleman</part> arrives at the manor and hangs his coat on the <part>coat hook</part> by the door. A butler is already there, bowing, pouring tea, polishing shoes. All day long, he is there to <kanji>attend</kanji> to every wish.
仕.on: The butler even polishes the gentleman's old <sound>shi</sound>eld until it gleams.
仕.kun: Dust makes the butler sneeze, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', but he keeps serving: next comes <sound>ca</sound>rp on a silver plate.

腹.meaning: Under a full <part>moon</part>, a man lies back in a <part>deck chair</part> after a huge dinner. His shirt buttons pop one by one, and his round middle rises like a second moon. Pat, pat: a very full <kanji>abdomen</kanji>.
腹.on: He hangs his tight belt on a <sound>hoo</sound>k and sighs with relief.
腹.kun: He pats his belly in a beach <sound>hu</sound>t while his friends cheer '<sound>Rah</sound>-rah!'

赤.meaning: A heap of <part>soil</part> sits on four little legs of flame, and the fire under it burns hotter and hotter. The earth glows like a brick in a kiln, then like a cherry, then like a stop sign. It's bright <kanji>red</kanji>.
赤.on: Cut the glowing heap like a pie chart, and every <sound>sec</sound>tor is red right through.
赤.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' you yelp, as a <sound>ca</sound>rp leaps out of the pond, red as a hot coal.

割.meaning: Two kids fight over one cake, and someone is about to come to <part>harm</part>. Mum steps in with a knife as sharp as a <part>dagger</part> and slices: a big piece for the big kid, a small one for the small kid. Each gets a fair <kanji>proportion</kanji>.
割.on: Then she cuts a crumbed <sound>katsu</sound> cutlet into the very same shares.
割.kun: The small kid wails '<sound>Wa</sound>h!' at his share and sulks off to snorkel on the coral <sound>ree</sound>f.

窓.meaning: You punch a <part>hole</part> in the wall of your room, lean your <part>elbow</part> on the edge and look out. The fresh air and the view of the hills lift your <part>heart</part>. Add a sheet of glass and you've made a <kanji>window</kanji>.
窓.on: Then you scrub the new glass with a big slippery bar of <sound>soa</sound>p.
窓.kun: You set a <sound>mu</sound>g on the sill and spot a <sound>do</sound>lphin leaping in the bay.

矢.meaning: A boy bounces on a <part>diving board</part> above a <part>large</part> target painted on the pool floor. He throws something small and feathered with a sharp tip, and it sails down and sticks right in the middle. Thunk: a <kanji>dart</kanji>.
矢.on: His next throw bounces off a knight's <sound>shi</sound>eld floating in the pool.
矢.kun: He ties a ball of <sound>ya</sound>rn to the dart so he can reel it back in.

医.meaning: A <part>drawer</part> slides open in the clinic, full of tiny needles, each shaped like a <part>dart</part>. The patient goes pale. 'Just a little prick,' says the one in the white coat, and it's over before you can say ouch. That's the <kanji>doctor</kanji>.
医.on: Next patient: an <sound>ee</sound>l with a sore throat, wriggling all over the table.
医.kun: One dart of medicine and the <sound>ee</sound>l is cured, swimming happily home: to heal.

知.meaning: A quiz host fires a question, and the answer shoots out of your <part>mouth</part> as fast as a <part>dart</part>, straight to the bullseye. No guessing, no 'um', no looking it up. You just <kanji>know</kanji>.
知.on: A <sound>chee</sound>tah in the next seat slams the buzzer even faster.
知.kun: The prize is a golden knight's <sound>shi</sound>eld with your name on it.

鉄.meaning: A miner digs for <part>gold</part>, but every nugget he finds he manages to <part>lose</part>: down a crack, into the river, through a hole in his pocket. All he has left is a heavy grey lump that won't go anywhere. Plain old <kanji>iron</kanji>.
鉄.on: He drops the lump in his fish tank, and a tiny <sound>tet</sound>ra fish sulks behind it.
鉄.kun: A <sound>cu</sound>ckoo, a <sound>ro</sound>dent, a bulb of <sound>ga</sound>rlic and a fishing <sound>ne</sound>t all end up stuck to his heavy lump.

塩.meaning: At the seaside you stand on a mound of <part>soil</part>, bounce off a <part>diving board</part> with your <part>mouth</part> wide open and swallow a gulp of sea water. Spluttering, you spit it into a <part>dish</part> and leave it in the sun. White crystals appear: <kanji>salt</kanji>.
塩.on: A fishing boat's <sound>en</sound>gine chugs past, its deck piled with sacks of salt.
塩.kun: A knight dips his <sound>shi</sound>eld in the dish, licks it and gasps: '<sound>Oh</sound>!'

音.meaning: You <part>stand</part> on a hill as the <part>sun</part> comes up, and it rings like a giant gong: bonnng! Birds wake, dogs bark, the whole valley hums. Every morning starts with that <kanji>sound</kanji>.
音.on: Someone flicks a big <sound>on</sound> switch, and the gong rings even louder.
音.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' you cover your ears as the sound bounces back off a <sound>to</sound>tem pole.

意.meaning: A tiny <part>chime</part> rings deep inside your <part>heart</part>: ding! You sit bolt upright in bed, eyes wide. Something new and bright has just popped into your head. It's an <kanji>idea</kanji>.
意.on: Your brilliant idea: teach an <sound>ee</sound>l to ring the chime with its tail.

注.meaning: The <part>lord</part> of the house holds out his cup, and a servant tips the jug. <part>Water drops</part> splash, the cup fills, spills over, and the floor shines. 'Stop!' says the lord, but she keeps going. She just loves to <kanji>pour</kanji>.
注.on: The lord tries to plug the jug with a wad of <sound>chew</sound>ing gum.
注.kun: The water pours onto one <sound>so</sound>fa, then the other <sound>so</sound>fa, soaking them both.

文.meaning: You write a line of words on a strip of paper, put the <part>lid</part> back on your pen, and snip the strip with <part>scissors</part> right after the full stop. Capital letter at the start, dot at the end: one whole <kanji>sentence</kanji>.
文.on: A ba<sound>boon</sound> grabs your strip of paper and reads it aloud, upside down.
文.kun: You tuck the strip under a <sound>fu</sound>ton for a <sound>mee</sound>rkat to find: a letter.

思.meaning: A farmer leans on his hoe at the edge of his <part>rice field</part>, one hand on his <part>heart</part>, staring at the rows. Plant now, or wait for rain? He doesn't move for an hour. He's busy: he has to <kanji>think</kanji>.
思.on: He scratches a plan in the mud with the edge of an old <sound>shi</sound>eld.
思.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>,' he mutters, tapping his <sound>mo</sound>ccasin in the mud, still thinking.
